title: Add AWS Private VPC Terraform alpha examples (minimal + enterprise locked-down) with walkthrough
author: Bruno Silva
body: Summary: Adds a complete AWS example for the alpha Terraform module set used by Redwood Private (VPC) deployments, including both (1) a minimal “getting started” topology and (2) an “enterprise locked-down” topology intended for customers with strict egress controls. Includes a README walkthrough, tfvars examples, and validation steps that align with installer networking preflight checks. Motivation: Solutions/PS and pilot customers need a copy/paste-able reference that demonstrates supported topologies and makes the module inputs/outputs concrete. The example repo is the lowest-friction way to keep docs + runnable configuration in sync during alpha. What’s included: (a) examples/aws/private-vpc-alpha/minimal: uses modules/redwood-private-vpc with defaults; supports single NAT or per-AZ NAT; enables required endpoints (ECR api/dkr, S3 gateway, CloudWatch Logs) and Route53 private DNS; (b) examples/aws/private-vpc-alpha/enterprise-locked-down: private-only subnets for workloads, optional no-public-egress mode (no IGW, no NAT) relying on VPC endpoints; tight SG defaults; explicit notes about requiring private DNS resolver behavior; (c) README.md: prerequisites, required IAM permissions, apply order, installer mapping (which outputs are consumed), validation commands, and teardown guidance; (d) scripts/validate.sh: lightweight wrapper to run terraform fmt/validate and a basic plan check. Notes/guardrails: This is an alpha reference; it intentionally does NOT cover multi-account networking, Transit Gateway routing, or bespoke proxy egress appliances beyond documented placeholders. The locked-down variant explicitly calls out that missing STS endpoint can break certain flows if the environment disallows public egress. Testing: validated with terraform 1.6.x and aws provider ~> 5.x in us-east-1 and us-west-2; CI runs fmt/validate + markdown lint. Follow-ups: once redwood-private-installer PR-388 lands everywhere, we should add a small section showing how to feed outputs into installer config verbatim (and keep it pinned to the stable output contract).
commits: examples/aws: add private-vpc-alpha skeleton + shared locals
minimal: working baseline example + outputs + tfvars.sample
enterprise: locked-down variant w/ private-only endpoints notes
docs: README walkthrough + validation + teardown steps
chore: add validate.sh + markdown lint config tweaks
conversation: Irene Choi (review): The locked-down variant currently mentions “no public egress” but still enables IGW in the diagram text. Please make this explicit: either IGW=false, NAT=false, and endpoints required, or separate into two sub-cases. Also add a note on NAT cost tradeoffs (single vs per-AZ) since customers ask constantly.

Bruno Silva (author): Good catch. Updated locked-down README to explicitly set enable_internet_gateway=false and nat_mode="disabled" for the no-egress case. Also added a short section in the top-level README on NAT modes and cost/support tradeoffs consistent with our alpha defaults.

Ethan Park (review): Can you add a “Installer mapping” snippet showing which outputs are required? Even if we can’t paste full installer config, at least list subnet_ids (private/isolated), vpc_endpoint_ids, and private_zone_id. This will reduce back-and-forth with PS.

Bruno Silva (author): Added “Mapping to redwood-private-installer” section listing the exact outputs consumed and where they go. I avoided pinning to a specific installer YAML schema, but included the names + meaning + preflight checks that will fail if missing.

Marcus Lin (review): Security note: locked-down variant should strongly recommend VPC Flow Logs (even if example doesn’t provision them) and should not suggest opening any inbound CIDRs on SGs. Also please remove “0.0.0.0/0 for debugging” language (even as a warning).

Bruno Silva (author): Removed the debugging CIDR language. Added an explicit security section: no inbound from 0.0.0.0/0, prefer SSM Session Manager/bastion patterns outside scope, and a callout that flow logs are part of the alpha secure defaults (with a pointer to the modules repo docs).

Elliot Price (review): Doc nit: Please align terminology with docs-site: use “Redwood Private (VPC)” consistently, and rename “enterprise locked-down” to “enterprise (restricted egress)” in headings. Also add quickstart-style numbered steps at the top.

Bruno Silva (author): Updated terminology + headings, and added a numbered quickstart at top-level README. Kept directory name as enterprise-locked-down for now to avoid churn, but README title and navigation use “enterprise (restricted egress)”.

Kira Thompson (review): Please add a short troubleshooting section for the two most common failures we’re seeing: (1) ECR pull failing due to missing endpoints/policy, and (2) DNS resolution of private endpoint names failing when private DNS is off. A couple of commands to validate would help.
Bruno Silva (author): Added troubleshooting + validation commands (dig/nslookup for endpoint names, curl to STS if egress allowed, and a note about checking route tables for the S3 gateway endpoint).

CI (system): terraform-validate (enterprise-locked-down) failed: Error creating VPC Endpoint: InvalidParameter: The vpcEndpointType Interface does not support the service in this region (temporary AWS API inconsistency)

Bruno Silva (author): Re-ran CI. This appears to be transient and matches the eventual consistency flake we’ve seen; no config change needed here. Will follow up to improve retry/backoff in module CI harness in the terraform repo.
Irene Choi (review): Re-review looks good. One more request: add an explicit “Supported by alpha” vs “Not supported (alpha)” table so customers don’t assume TGW/multi-account is included.
Bruno Silva (author): Added a small table under “Scope and non-goals (alpha)” in README. Thanks.
Marcus Lin (review): Approved after the CIDR/debug language removal + security callouts. Please keep the locked-down sample as the first link we send to regulated prospects.
Elliot Price (review): Approved. I’ll mirror the quickstart structure on the docs site.
Ethan Park (review): Approved. Installer mapping section is exactly what we needed.
release_notes: Added runnable AWS reference examples for Terraform modules alpha (minimal + enterprise restricted-egress) with a README walkthrough, validation steps, and installer output mapping.
